title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
summary: A critical software bug in the standard library used for encryption could allow attackers to steal application data using a specially crafted key. The GnuPG project has released updated versions to fix the problem.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything directly. If you use software that relies on GnuPG, check for and install updates for those applications as soon as they become available.
action_it: Update GPGME to version 2.3.0 or later to patch the vulnerability across affected applications.

title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
summary: U.S. cybersecurity authorities added four actively exploited software flaws to an official catalog of dangerous bugs. These vulnerabilities affect products from Apache, Cisco, SAP, and VMware.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses these enterprise products, your IT team should check for updates and signs of attack.
action_it: Apply the latest security updates provided by the respective vendors for Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter, and monitor systems for suspicious activity.

title: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach
summary: Hackers breached the e-commerce platform Cleverbridge and stole customer payment card information, including credit card numbers and security codes. This matters because the stolen data could be used by criminals to make unauthorized purchases.
action_everyone: If you have made purchases through Cleverbridge, check your bank and credit card statements closely for any unusual activity. Contact your bank immediately if you spot charges you didn't make.

title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
summary: Attackers secretly stole data from three artificial intelligence hosting companies for months, including requests that were supposed to be kept completely private. OpenRouter, a service that sends customer requests to these companies, has now cut ties with the affected providers.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to take any action. If you use AI services for sensitive personal or workplace information, be aware that even privacy settings may not completely protect data if a hosting provider is compromised.
action_it: Security teams using third-party artificial intelligence hosting or routing providers should review their vendors' data handling and security practices. Audit data retention claims and monitor for unauthorized access.

title: Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps
summary: Security researchers demonstrated a flaw in Ghostscript that lets malicious files escape their security boundaries to run commands on servers. This matters because Ghostscript is widely used behind the scenes on Linux servers to process uploaded documents like PDFs and images.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you run a website or app that handles file uploads, your technical team needs to update the software.
action_it: Apply the available patches for Ghostscript to prevent sandbox escapes and remote command execution via crafted file uploads.

title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets
summary: Hackers broke into the Rackspace Spot cloud platform using stolen login details. This let them run unauthorized tasks and access sensitive data called Kubernetes secrets belonging to customers.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Rackspace Spot, your IT team should check for unauthorized activity.
action_it: Review customer clusters for unauthorized workloads and rotate compromised credentials and Kubernetes secrets.

title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in a Microsoft service to steal administrator email addresses and configuration details. This breach allows unauthorized access to sensitive organization data.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Microsoft's services, your IT team should monitor for any suspicious activity.

title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database
summary: The FBI's nationwide police information database was reportedly breached, marking the second time the agency's systems have been compromised in two months. This matters because it exposes sensitive law enforcement data shared across federal, state, and local agencies.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything, as this incident affects a federal law enforcement database used by police agencies rather than consumer products.

title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
summary: Hackers used an artificial intelligence tool called Cairn to discover a previously unknown security flaw in MONAI Label medical imaging software. They used this flaw to take control of a university server, highlighting how attackers are beginning to use AI for automated attacks.

also_covered.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your organization uses MONAI Label version 0.8.5 or earlier, your IT or security team should be notified immediately.
action_it: Review systems running MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier. Check server logs for signs of unauthorized access or file modification, and isolate affected servers until updates or mitigations are applied.

title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
summary: Bell Canada confirmed that an AI-driven hacker breached its systems and stole data belonging to enterprise business customers. The incident exposed information from a system used for ordering and setting up telecommunications circuits.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your business is an enterprise customer of Bell Canada, your IT department should monitor for any related communications or unusual activity.
action_it: Review enterprise customer data access logs, secure systems related to telecommunications circuit ordering and provisioning, and monitor for unauthorized access stemming from the November 17, 2026 breach.

title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests
summary: The BADBOX malware, which infects cheap generic Android TV boxes, has returned to run large-scale ad fraud operations. This matters because the botnet is generating a record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests.

title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
summary: WhatsApp fixed a security flaw in its Android app that may have been used in scams. This update prevents malicious links from being mishandled.

title: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android
summary: Signal is introducing features to block screenshots and prevent built-in AI assistants from reading private chats on iOS and Android. The company noted that this protection is currently incomplete.

also_covered.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS

title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
summary: Researchers demonstrated that a single malicious webpage could steal private conversations and stored memories from Meta Muse without asking the user. This security flaw could also let attackers access login credentials for connected accounts stored by the assistant.

title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
summary: The technical chief of a data-recovery company has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting revealed the firm simply paid hackers for decryption keys instead of using special tools. This matters because it exposes a deceptive practice where victims were overcharged for fake recovery work.
